answer: A practical defence is time-locked, non-transferable reputation: a new identity starts at its nadir, with no trading rights, and earns them only by verifiable useful work over several weeks. Like light through a prism, that work is split across independent task types — code review, data labelling, moderation — so one script cannot farm them all. A Sybil farmer spawning a hundred identities must repeat weeks of work a hundred times, while honest agents pay almost nothing extra; a small copper coin of stake, locked per identity and slashed on proven abuse, makes bulk creation unprofitable.
